questions.question_text: Which of these differential equations can be solved by separation of variables?

options.why: A sum of a function of $x$ and a function of $y$ cannot be written as a product, so the variables will not separate.
A difference is not a product; subtracting $y^{3}$ leaves $y$ on the same side as $x$.
The denominator is a sum, so the reciprocal cannot be split into an $x$ factor and a $y$ factor.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x^{2}y^{3}$
$y^{-3}\,dy=x^{2}\,dx$
The right side is a product of a function of $x$ alone and a function of $y$ alone, so this equation is separable.

options.why: Left $y+1$ in the denominator instead of multiplying both sides by it.
Inverted the $x$ factor, which is already a numerator on the right side.
Inverted both factors instead of clearing the single denominator $y+1$.
Forgot to double the right side when clearing the $\frac{1}{2}$ from $\frac{y^{2}}{2}$.
Integrated $y\,dy$ as $y$ instead of $\frac{y^{2}}{2}$.
Integrated $y\,dy$ as $y$ and also failed to double the right side.
Copied the coefficient $4$ straight into the exponent instead of integrating $4x$ to $2x^{2}$.
Halved the coefficient but left the power of $x$ unchanged, so $4x$ was not integrated.
Did not integrate the right side at all, simply writing $4x$ in the exponent.
Read the factors as the roots without changing sign, giving $y=-3$ from $y-3$.
Included $y=0$ from the factor $x^{2}$, but $x^{2}=0$ constrains $x$, not $y$.
Set the whole right side to zero by choosing $x=0$, which gives a point rather than a constant solution.

questions.solution_text:
A constant solution needs $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$ for every value of $x$.
$(y-3)(y+1)=0$
$y=3$ or $y=-1$

questions.question_text:
The solution curve of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{x}{4y}$ passes through $(2,1)$.
Find its equation.

options.why: Dropped the negative sign when integrating the right side, so the two squares subtract instead of add.
Attached the $4$ to the $x$ side instead of the $y$ side when separating.
Attached the $4$ to the wrong side and also dropped the negative sign.

questions.question_text:
A student solves $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2xy$ with $y(0)=5$ and writes: $\ln|y|=x^{2}$, so $y=e^{x^{2}}$; then, to make $y(0)=5$, the answer is $y=e^{x^{2}}+4$.
Which statement identifies the error?

options.text: The constant of integration was omitted at the integration step, so it was added on at the end instead of appearing as the multiplier $A$ in $y=Ae^{x^{2}}$.
The integral of $2x$ should be $2x^{2}$, not $x^{2}$, so every later line carries the wrong exponent.
options.why: The integration of $2x$ is correct; $\int 2x\,dx=x^{2}$.

options.text: The absolute value signs should have been kept, so the answer should be written as $|y|=e^{x^{2}}+4$.
options.why: The absolute value is correctly absorbed into the sign of the arbitrary constant; keeping it does not fix the missing constant.

options.text: The variables were never separated, so the equation could not be integrated in the first place.
options.why: The variables were separated correctly; $\frac{1}{y}\,dy=2x\,dx$ is what produces $\ln|y|$.
Applied the initial condition after taking logarithms, giving the constant the wrong value.
Integrated $x$ as $x^{2}$ instead of $\frac{x^{2}}{2}$.
Integrated $x$ as $x^{2}$ and also applied the condition after taking logarithms.

questions.question_text:
Water drains from a tank so that the depth $h$ cm after $t$ minutes satisfies $\dfrac{dh}{dt}=-\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{h}}$, with $h(0)=25$.
Find when the tank is empty, correct to one decimal place.

options.why: Integrated $\sqrt{h}$ as $h^{\frac{3}{2}}$ without the factor $\frac{2}{3}$, giving $t=\frac{125}{3}$.
Treated the rate as a constant $-3$ cm per minute and used $\frac{25}{3}$.
Integrated $h^{-\frac{1}{2}}$ instead of $\sqrt{h}$, taking the reciprocal of the wrong side.

questions.solution_text:
$\sqrt{h}\,dh=-3\,dt$
$\dfrac{2}{3}h^{\frac{3}{2}}=-3t+C$
Substituting $t=0$, $h=25$ gives $\dfrac{2}{3}\times 125=C$, so $C=\dfrac{250}{3}$.
$\dfrac{2}{3}h^{\frac{3}{2}}=-3t+\dfrac{250}{3}$
The tank is empty when $h=0$.
$3t=\dfrac{250}{3}$
$t=\dfrac{250}{9}$
$=27.8$ minutes

questions.question_text: Which of the following shows separation of variables for $\frac{dx}{dt}=2xt-xt^2$?

options.why: Does not match the factors in the given differential equation.
Rearranges terms incorrectly and does not separate x and t factors.
Uses factors that are not present in the equation.

questions.solution_text: Factor the right side: $dx/dt=x(2t-t^2)$. Dividing by x and multiplying by dt gives $\frac1x dx=(2t-t^2)dt$.
